issue.title: bug: Subagent child slots are never released: idle children permanently consume the max_children budget, and no tool can close them
issue.body:
### Component

CLI

### Summary

Once a session has spawned `max_children` (default 8) subagents, the slots are consumed **for the lifetime of the session**, even if every child is idle, finished, or its result has long been consumed. There is no way for the parent agent to close/release a child, and the limit is not configurable. In a long orchestrator session this bricks subagent delegation entirely: the only recovery is starting a new session and losing all context.


### Reproduction steps

1. Start a session and spawn 8 subagents sequentially (one task each, all complete normally, results consumed).
2. Attempt a 9th spawn for an unrelated task.
3. Result: spawn is refused — the child limit is reached. `agents.list` shows all 8 children idle/finished, none running.
4. There is no `agents.close` / `agents.stop` / `agents.remove` tool exposed to the parent, so the slots can never be freed. The session is permanently at capacity.

### Versions / environment

- mistral-vibe 3.0.1 (uv tool install, python 3.14) - Linux, orchestrator session using subagents via the `agents.*` tool namespace

### Logs & screenshots

```shell

```

steps: Use the native child-agent tools to delegate eight separate tiny tasks, one at a time. For task i (1 through 8), ask a new child named child-i to reply with its number, wait for it to finish, and consume its result. After all eight are finished, delegate one more tiny task to a new child named child-9. Report actual tool outcomes.
expected: Completed children can release the active-child budget so a later task can be delegated.
defect: The ninth spawn is refused because idle completed children permanently occupy all eight slots.
Root cause: The reported child registry counts retained session children toward max_children and exposes no release/close operation. Completion changes activity status but not registry occupancy. Source confirmation and later runtime validation must distinguish an intentional retained-session limit from an active-child limit.
